A seat sits on a salt cavern holding gas. The operator files its id and casing record; the node reads the state register, rejects a second seat there, and reads twelve months of injection telemetry. Salt creeps, so the cavity passes a mechanical integrity test every five years, ferrous casing tested against brine. Gas cycling leaves a ripple no copied name reproduces.

Leaching one runs three years: 900,000 barrels of brine, drilling 4.5 million dollars, compressors 1.1 million, permits 300,000. Fifty clones pay 300 million to wait.

Salt is the vault, closing on any hollow nothing fills.
